name: Stewed Apples No. 1
description: Historical recipe from The Whitehouse Cookbook (1887). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: loaf sugar for every twelve apples
ingredients.originalText: a cupful of loaf sugar for every twelve apples

instructions.text: Take a dozen green tart apples, core and slice them
Put into a saucepan with just enough water to cover them
Cover the saucepan closely, and stew the apples until they are tender and clear
Take them out, put them into a deep dish and cover them
Add to the juice in the saucepan a cupful of loaf sugar for every twelve apples, and boil it half an hour
Add to the syrup a pinch of mace and a dozen whole cloves just ten minutes before taking from the fire
Pour scalding hot over the apples and set them in a cold place
Eat ice cold with cream or boiled custard

source.author: F.L. Gillette
source.originalInstructions:
1. Take a dozen green tart apples, core and slice them
2. Put into a saucepan with just enough water to cover them
3. Cover the saucepan closely, and stew the apples until they are tender and clear
4. Take them out, put them into a deep dish and cover them
5. Add to the juice in the saucepan a cupful of loaf sugar for every twelve apples, and boil it half an hour
6. Add to the syrup a pinch of mace and a dozen whole cloves just ten minutes before taking from the fire
7. Pour scalding hot over the apples and set them in a cold place
8. Eat ice cold with cream or boiled custard
